title: Cozy RTS with 10 clans, online multiplayer and an Android app, made entirely with AI tools (trailer + workflow)
author: FluffyBugGames
selftext:
I'm an artist, not a programmer, and for the past couple of weeks I've been building **Scutterfluff: Turf Wars**, a cozy RTS where fluffy animals fight bugs. Trailer above. Here's the full AI stack, since this sub is all about the how.

**Code: Claude Code**  
It writes 100% of the code. The game is three.js in the browser, plus the online multiplayer lobby, Google sign-in with cloud saves, an Android app and auto updates. I describe features, test on my phone and send screenshots back. Big systems like a whole new faction or a 3v3 hero battle mode come together surprisingly fast. Pixel-level UI polish takes the longest.

**Running several AI sessions in parallel**  
The game-changer was running multiple Claude sessions at once, one per feature. That only worked once I added rules:

* each build claims a version number
* builds stack on the latest live version
* every build gets a full regression test on a real GPU before I deploy

Without those rules, features kept overwriting each other.

**Art: ChatGPT → Meshy**  
ChatGPT makes the concepts, then a T-pose sheet and a props sheet, and Meshy turns those into 3D. A written style guide pasted every time keeps 10 clans looking like one game.

**The part nobody mentions**  
Generated models are never game ready: 7-legged spiders, fused wings, floating bags. Claude built me a little in-browser model viewer to sculpt, paint and pose fixes by hand.

**Performance**  
AI happily writes code that melts phones. I had a crash from GPU memory leaking every time a unit died, and the AI found it by profiling once I described the symptoms. A new horde mode now runs 600 critters on a weak laptop chip thanks to instancing.

**What's in now:** 10 clans, Classic RTS (bots or online), Hero Clash 3v3, cosmetics with no pay to win, progress synced between phone and PC. Next up is a roguelite survivor mode.

Free to play in the browser and on Android, link in the comments. Happy to answer anything about the workflow!
